input.quote: thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Computed parameters (spelled out in words in the document, restated numerically here): non-renewal notice window = 30 days ("thirty days'"), which is within both the preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day limits and far short of the 90-day walk-away threshold; renewal term = 12 months ("twelve-month"), i.e. annual and not multi-year; Vendor reminder = 60 days ("sixty days") before renewal, with the opt-out deadline extended to 30 days after a late reminder is received, so the short window cannot be lost through Vendor inaction; price uplift cap = lesser of CPI and 3% ("three percent") with 90 days' ("ninety days'") notice and no increase applied to prepaid periods. The opt-out is Customer-only, so Vendor has no reciprocal non-renewal lever. § 8.1's 3-year figure is a fixed initial term, not an automatic multi-year renewal, and does not extend the Order Form opt-out window. All preferred parameters are met; no redline needed.
